Mr. Kirudja, I understood the question of Mr. Knoops to be whether Mr. Stanisic ever expressed, especially in view of his sensitive position within the government, whether he expressed any fear to be the subject of aggression from within his own government circles, whereas your answer appears to focus primarily on aggression against Serbia by NATO and concerns about that. Now, I'm trying to fully understand whether what you told us was on the basis of an accurate understanding of what Mr. Knoops asked you. First of all, Mr. Knoops, did I summarise the question in an accurate way?

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: You did, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kirudja, have I misunderstood you if your answer was very much focusing on consequences for Serbia and aggression against Serbia rather than fear expressed by Mr. Stanisic for becoming a subject of aggression within his own government circles?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, first my apology for causing you some misunderstanding, but I do think you have summarised accurately part of what I intended to convey. The part you have summarised, that fear in general from the threat of NATO strike, that's correct. I meant in my earlier answer to tell you, Your Honour, he did, by deduction, imply the fear that he felt in undertaking this mission. Not because he said it was coming directly from his government, as the question was put. He expressed it as an inherent fear based on that threat that members not only within his government, some members within his government and others in this community or group that, "if I don't," he seemed to say, "If I don't tell them I have obtained an undertaking from the UN that there won't be retaliatory strikes and I go there asking for release of these hostages, don't you see," he hinted, "I could very much lose some of them as well as my own security." That's what I intended to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It's clear to me now. Please proceed, Mr. Knoops.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: In line with the question or your explanation to Dr. Kirudja, did Mr. Stanisic at any moment express fear for his own position within his service?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES KIRUDJA
utterances.text: That one, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Knoops. Mr. Domazet, and I'm also addressing you, Mr. Simatovic, if I understood you well, you feel that you're not in a position to cross-examine Mr. Kirudja. Is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it is, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber, at this moment, does not judge upon the question whether the opportunity given to you now to cross-examine Mr. Kirudja, whether for good reasons you didn't use it or for reasons which would not justify to remain passive at this moment. As I said before, we'll further consider that matter in view of -- of what we'll hear. Mr. Kirudja, this is a matter you're not familiar with and you shouldn't bother about, but it is a procedural aspect at this moment which you'll not be able to understand without any further information which I'm not going to give you, because the Chamber will have to deal with it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, the Chamber has no questions for Mr. Kirudja. Is there any need to re-examine Mr. Kirudja?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Groome --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I thought I heard my name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I express my feelings of thanks to you, and it's of course good that you get up immediately. No, no, no. It's -- Mr. Kirudja, I nevertheless will express a few things to you. We are in a situation where the Simatovic Defence has expressed that it finds itself not in a position at this moment to meaningfully cross-examine you for reasons unfamiliar to you and familiar to the Chamber. The Chamber will further consider that matter and whether this is a lost opportunity for the Simatovic Defence, or whether there were reasons for them to refrain from cross-examining you at this moment, which also means that the possibility, and I'm emphasising "possibility," is still open that in the future this Chamber might decide that the proceedings would not be fair to Mr. Simatovic if no additional opportunity would be given to him to cross-examine you. That's uncertain moment, but it causes me - and that's a bit unusual for someone who is excused at that very moment - it causes me to ask you not to speak with anyone about the testimony you've given, because there still is a possibility that you would be further cross-examined on the examination-in-chief and that further questions may be put to you in relation to the cross-examination already conducted by Mr. Knoops. So therefore, that might take some time. That could be weeks or even months. I instruct you not it speak to anyone during this longer period of time about your testimony. Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I just raise a concern that I'm sure some of my colleagues on the Karadzic case and the Mico Stanisic case are probably thinking about now. Could I ask if the Office of the Prosecutor takes appropriate measures that no one on the Jovica Stanisic case or Franko Simatovic case has any contact with Mr. Kirudja, that members in unrelated cases may be able to contact him, to interview him in matters unrelated to this case?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You want to create a Chinese wall --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: As it were, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- between you and your colleagues. The circumstances are exceptional. The need to speak with Mr. Kirudja within the next few days does not arise, I take it, and the Chamber understood, Mr. Kirudja, that you're leaving Holland rather soon. The Chamber will give further instructions to you as far as this aspect is concerned, perhaps also after having heard any submissions by the Defence. Well, say within the next 14 days.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Kirudja, then we've come to the point where I would like to thank you very much for coming to The Hague and for answering questions put to you by the parties and by the Bench. And I usually wish witnesses a safe trip home again. I don't know whether you're heading for home or not, but at least wherever you go, arrive there safely.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Usher, could you please escort Mr. Kirudja out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Earlier today I explained to you, Mr. Simatovic, and to you, Mr. Domazet, that an ex parte hearing would need some preparation, which was not easily done just in the middle of an ordinary court session. Since we've now done, as matters stand now, with the testimony of Mr. Kirudja, the Chamber would prefer to already have these ex parte hearing today. For that purpose we would need a bit of a longer break, that is, approximately a half an hour, and then we would still have available a little bit over one hour for this ex parte hearing. The Chamber has requested OLAD to be stand by to join in that hearing, which would mean that that hearing would take place in the absence of the Stanisic Defence and in the absence of the Prosecution, and it would be a hearing in closed session. Then for those parties who will not participate in the ex parte hearing, we will resume tomorrow at a quarter past 2.00 in the afternoon for you, and for Mr. Domazet and Mr. Simatovic, an ex parte will be held in 30 minutes from now in this same courtroom. Any procedural issues to be raised at this moment? Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: None. Mr. Knoops? None. Then we adjourn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be followed by an Ex Parte Hearing. The hearing will reconvened on Thursday, the 27th day of August, 2009, at 2.15 p.m. 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 5.05 p.m.,
